title: Unassigned is always the first group in Tech View
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view (check in Settings > Roles & Permissions > open your role > Work Orders section). The Admin role has both.
  2. Use a desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  3. In the top bar, choose the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Create everything below in this location.
  4. Make sure the location has the technicians this case uses (e.g. "Esther Howard", "Ralph Edwards" and "Jenny Wilson"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff record is Active, Clockable is on, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member > enter the first and last name (e.g. Esther Howard), role Technician, Clockable on, Active, enrolled at this location > Save.
  5. Create the work orders this case uses and set their lead technician (e.g. S1-352 and S1-355 with no lead, others led by Esther Howard and Ralph Edwards):
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose the customer "ZZAUTOTEST Unassigned First" (add it with the Add button in the customer box if it does not exist; using it keeps this test's work orders apart from others at the location) and an asset (e.g. unit TRK-118, 2022 Freightliner M2) > Create. Write down the number the build gives the work order (the numbers in this case are examples).
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician (e.g. Esther Howard) and save. Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. Click Search and type ZZAUTOTEST Unassigned First so only this test's work orders show.
  4. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (in the design its tooltip reads "By Lead Tech").
  5. Look at which group is at the top of the table and what it contains.
  6. Drag the Esther Howard group by its header handle (tooltip "Drag to reorder technicians") above the Unassigned group and let go.
  7. Look at which group is at the top again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The first group is Unassigned, before every technician group, and it holds exactly your work orders with no lead (e.g. S1-352 and S1-355).
  • After the drag, Unassigned is still first: Esther Howard's group lands after it, never above it.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View — table grouped by lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S2-R2, read 8 Oct 2026. Design: Claude Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Work Orders.dc.html), By Lead Tech, Unassigned group and drag handle; on-screen labels only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R2: “Keep Unassigned, containing work orders without a lead technician, fixed before all technician groups.”
